briefing.headline: Harbour’s high press and left-sided attack lost momentum after the break; Kestrel recovered territory and levelled the game

first_half.text: Harbour controlled territory by attacking strongly down the left and pressing high, shown by a dominant left-channel share of 70.6% and frequent left-channel entries (2.67 per_window), plus an aggressive PPDA of 3.3.
That control translated into real offensive output: more final-third entries (3.78 per_window) and xG (0.75), and they converted one of those chances (1 goal in the first half).
Kestrel were pushed wide and struggled to win the ball high, registering few high regains (0.33 per_window) and limited attacking entries overall (right-channel entries 0.78 per_window).

changes.text: Kestrel clawed back territory after the break: their possession rose slightly to 45.4% (from 44.7%) and their centre and right-channel entries increased (centre 0.44→1.33 per_window, right 0.78→1 per_window), giving them more access through central and right channels.

Harbour eased their press and lost some attacking momentum: their PPDA rose from 3.3 to 4.4 (a 33% increase) and left-channel activity dropped (left entries 2.67→1.56 per_window; left share 70.6%→53.8%), reducing the dominance they showed early on.
Kestrel ramped their final-third threat: their final-third entries rose from 1.33 to 2.56 per_window and xG went from 0.04 to 1.01, producing a productive second half.

predictions.text: Prediction that Harbour would protect their left and reduce Kestrel’s right access was contradicted: Kestrel's right-channel entries rose from 0.78 to 1 per_window after the break.
Prediction that Harbour’s PPDA would rise as they eased pressing was confirmed: PPDA rose from 3.3 to 4.4 (a 33% increase).
Prediction that Harbour would maintain or increase final-third entries was contradicted: their final-third entries fell from 3.78 to 2.89 per_window after the break.
Prediction that Kestrel would force down Harbour’s left-channel access was confirmed: Harbour's left-channel entries dropped from 2.67 to 1.56 per_window (a 42% decrease).

Prediction that Kestrel dropping a midfielder would cut Harbour’s high regains was contradicted: Harbour's high regains per_window fell only from 2.11 to 2, a 5% change, far short of the predicted drop.
Prediction that Kestrel would significantly increase overall possession was contradicted: their possession rose only from 44.7 to 45.4% (a 2% change), well below the forecasted 10% rise.

result.text: Kestrel’s second-half territorial recovery and increased final-third entries produced higher xG and ultimately an equaliser: Kestrel’s final-third entries rose to 2.56 per_window and xG to 1.01, and they scored in the second half.

Harbour’s early control delivered an opening goal thanks to left-sided dominance and high pressing, but easing their press and a drop in left-channel attacks reduced their threat after the break (final-third entries fell to 2.89 per_window), leaving them with a draw.
Overall the match ended level as Kestrel’s tactical adjustments regained enough territory and chance volume to offset Harbour’s first-half advantage, reflected in the 1-1 final scoreline.
